item.description: PTC India on Monday posted a more than 28 per cent fall in consolidated net profit to Rs 159.10 crore in the September quarter, mainly on account of increased expenses. It had clocked a net profit of Rs 222.05 crore in the second quarter of the preceding financial year, the company said in an exchange filing. During the second quarter of FY27, the company's total income, however, increased to Rs 5,958.24 crore from Rs 5,585.21 crore in the year-ago period. Total expenses increased to Rs 5,788.97 crore from Rs 5,287.25 crore in the July-September period FY26. In a statement, PTC India said its trading volume grew by 24 per cent to 32.46 BUs (billion units) in Q2 FY27 on a standalone basis. item.description: IPO-bound PRISM, parent entity of hospitality chain OYO, has posted a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 353 crore in the first quarter ended June, registering 17 per cent growth from Rs 301 crore in the year-ago period. The quarterly profit included a deferred-tax credit of approximately Rs 244 crore, according to the company's audited financials seen by PTI. PRISM's revenue from operations increased 35 per cent to Rs 2,814 crore in the first quarter of FY2026-27, compared with Rs 2,078 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, the audited financials showed. The company's Gross Booking Value grew 30 per cent to nearly Rs 9,600 crore in the same period. Growth was broad-based across its hotels and vacation homes businesses. PRISM's hotel segment bookings grew 30 per cent year-on-year, while the vacation homes business recorded 28 per cent growth in bookings. item.title: Ambani tops Forbes' billionaire gainers list with $6.3 bn wealth jump
item.description: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani has emerged as the world's biggest billionaire wealth gainer, adding over USD 6 billion to his fortune in a single day, as shares of his flagship company surged following a stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings performance. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires list, Ambani's wealth increased by 7.85 per cent, or USD 6.3 billion, making him the biggest gainer globally in the latest update to the ranking on November 2. The gain was substantially ahead of the second-biggest wealth accretion on the list, with Spanish retail billionaire Amancio Ortega adding USD 1.7 billion, followed by China's Zhong Shanshan at USD 1.5 billion. The gains pushed Ambani to No.23 spot on the world billionaire list, making him the richest Indian ahead of Gautam Adani, who was ranked at No.26 with a wealth of USD 79.12 billion, according to the Forbes listing. Ambani had a wealth of USD 88.8 billion, according to Forbes. The sharp increase in Ambani's ..

item.title: ED registers money laundering case against Subhash Chandra over loan fraud
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate has registered a money laundering case against media baron Subhash Chandra in connection with an alleged loan fraud that caused a Rs 1,322 crore loss to Life Insurance Corporation Housing Finance Limited (LICHFL), officials said on Monday. Chandra is alleged to have inflated his net worth to avail loans from LICHFL and then defaulted on them. The officials said the case has been filed under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), taking cognisance of a CBI FIR. A comment from Chandra is awaited. The CBI had earlier filed a case on the complaint of LICHFL, based on which the ED registered the money laundering case. The LICHFL, in its complaint, which is part of the CBI FIR, alleged that Chandra submitted net-worth certificates used to secure the approval and disbursal of two loans totalling Rs 980 crore. item.title: Solex Energy eyeing US market for international debut, says chairman
item.description: Eyeing a footprint in the global renewable energy market, homegrown Solex Energy plans to establish solar module and cell manufacturing capacities in the US as part of its USD 1.5 billion investment roadmap through 2030. In an interaction, the company's Chairman Chetan Shah said that while the US remains the largest global solar market, steep anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports leave India as the sole viable supplier of low-cost alternatives. When asked whether Solex Energy is exploring expansion in the US, he replied in the affirmative. Sharing the rationale behind the move, he said Solex Energy is targeting the US market for expansion primarily to capitalise on the massive global demand for clean energy components while positioning itself as a reliable, cost-effective alternative to Chinese suppliers. "The US is a high-potential market. While many Indian corporates are already present there, a healthy number of business houses, including us, are also looking to invest there,"

item.title: IL&FS approaches NCLT to recover ₹186 crore excess pay from ex-directors

In an application filed before the Mumbai Bench of the NCLT, IL&FS has sought directions to its former directors and two key subsidiaries, IL&FS Financial Services (IFIN) and IL&FS Transportation Networks (ITNL), to return the excess remuneration. item.title: Sarda Energy & Minerals Q2 results: Net profit dips 2.2% to ₹320 crore
item.description: Sarda Energy & Minerals has reported a 2.2 per cent decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 320 crore, mainly impacted by lower revenues. It clocked Rs 328 crore profit after tax (PAT) in the second quarter of the preceding 2025-26 financial year, the company said in a statement on Saturday. In July-September, the company's total income reduced by 5.7 per cent to Rs 1,505 crore from Rs 1,596 crore a year ago. In Q2 FY2, the company's EBITDA also fell 2.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 564 crore from Rs 580 crore in July-September of FY26. However, in April-September, its PAT grew 4.5 per cent to Rs 799 crore from Rs 764 crore in the year-ago period. Sarda Energy & Minerals Limited (SEML) is an integrated energy and minerals company with interests spanning power generation, mining, steel and ferro alloys.
